# TASI API overview

Compact list of the public classes and functions of `tasi`, generated from the
code. Full documentation: https://tasi.readthedocs.io (or `help(obj)`).

## Concepts

- **Tabular core:** `Pose`, `Trajectory` and the `Dataset` classes are `pandas.DataFrame`
  subclasses with a `(timestamp, id)` row index and multi-level columns such as
  `("position", "easting")` or `("boundingbox", "center", "northing")`. Positions are UTM
  coordinates. All pandas methods work on them.
- **Hierarchy:** a `TrajectoryDataset` contains many traffic participants,
  `TrajectoryDataset.trajectory(id)` returns one `Trajectory`, and a `Trajectory` consists of
  `Pose` rows. The `Geo*` variants are `geopandas` based and add shapely geometries.
- **Public models (`tasi.io`):** pydantic models (`PosePublic`, `TrajectoryPublic`, ...) to
  exchange data, e.g. `TrajectoryPublic.from_tasi(trajectory)` and back with `.as_tasi()`.
- **ORM (`tasi.io.orm`):** SQLAlchemy models of the same entities. Tables use the placeholder
  schema `schema`, which only resolves through an engine from
  `DatabaseSettings().create_engine()` (settings from `TASI_ORM_*` variables or `.tasiorm`).
- **Safety metrics:** `trajectory.smos.pet(other)` returns a `tasi.smos.PET`.

## Extras

The base package only needs `numpy` and `pandas`. Modules that need an extra raise an
`ImportError` naming it.

| Extra | Enables |
|---|---|
| `geo` | `Geo*` classes (geopandas, shapely) |
| `io` | `tasi.io`, `tasi.io.orm`, `tasi.smos` (pydantic, SQLAlchemy) |
| `database` | PostgreSQL driver (psycopg) for `tasi.io.orm` |
| `visualization` | `tasi.plotting` (matplotlib) |
| `wms` | `tasi.plotting.wms` (map tiles) |
| `performance` | numba in `tasi.calculus` |
| `dtw` | `TrafficLightDataset.synchronize` (dtaidistance) |
| `download` | `tasi.dlr` |
| `osi` | `tasi.io.osi` |
| `all` | everything |

Signatures below omit `self`. Members marked *(property)* are attributes.

### `class DLRDatasetManager`

A base class for DLR dataset management

- `DLRDatasetManager(version: str, path: str = '<site-packages>/tasi/dataset/data', download_chunk_size: int = 1024, **kwargs)`
- `archivename` *(property)* — The base name of the archive
- `filename` *(property)* — The full name of the archive including the version
- `url` *(property)* — The URL to download the dataset from
- `version` *(property)* — The dataset version
- `name` *(property)*
- `download(file: _io.TextIOWrapper) -> int`
- `extract(file: pathlib.Path, path: pathlib.Path)`
- `load(path: pathlib.Path = None) -> str` — Download a specified DLR dataset.
- `trajectory(path: pathlib.Path = None) -> List[str]` — List of files with trajectory data.
- `weather(path: pathlib.Path = None) -> List[str]` — List of files with weather data.
- `road_condition(path: pathlib.Path = None) -> List[str]` — List of files with road condition information.
- `traffic_volume(path: pathlib.Path = None) -> List[str]` — List of files with traffic volume data.
- `openscenario(path: pathlib.Path = None) -> List[str]` — List of files with OpenSCENARIO data.

### `class BoundingboxPlotter(tilemapbase.Plotter)`

A specialization of the `tilemapbase.Plotter` to show tiles given a region as a boundingbox in UTM coordinates.

- `BoundingboxPlotter(extent: numpy.ndarray, tile_provider: BoundingboxTiles, padding: int = 0)`
- `plot(ax: matplotlib.Axes, position: Optional[Tuple[float, float]] = None, zoom: float = 1, show_attribution: bool = True, attribution_kwargs=None, **kwargs)` — Draw the tile for the position position given by ``position`` within the current extend and and zoom into the tile according to `zoom`.
- `extent` *(property)* — The region in 2-point definition
- `xtilemin` *(property)* — The smallest x-coordinate in tilespace
- `xtilemax` *(property)* — The greatest x-coordinate in tilespace
- `ytilemin` *(property)* — The smallest y-coordinate in tilespace
- `ytilemax` *(property)* — The greatest y-coordinate in tilespace

- `width` *(property)*
- `height` *(property)*
- `get_tile(x1, y1, x2, y2)`
- Attributes: `ATTRIBUTION`, `DEFAULT_PARAMS`, `SOURCE_NAME`, `WMS`
